stem.text: Find the particular solution to the differential equation \( \frac{dy}{dx} = \sqrt{x^{4} + 1} \) with the initial condition \( y(3) = -1 \), written in terms of a definite integral.

worked_solution.text: The right side depends on x alone and has no elementary antiderivative, so accumulate it from the initial input: \( \int_{3}^{x} \sqrt{t^{4} + 1}\,dt \) is the change in y from x = 3.
Add the initial value: \( y = -1 + \int_{3}^{x} \sqrt{t^{4} + 1}\,dt \), which equals \( -1 \) at x = 3 and has derivative \( \sqrt{x^{4} + 1} \).
worked_solution.rule_named: initial value plus the accumulated change

options.label: \( y = -1 + \int_{3}^{x} \sqrt{t^{4} + 1} \)
options.derivation: the initial value and the integral written with the differential dt left off
